claim: The prepared Grainfield process path is allocation-free across the declared 64/256/1024 block-size matrix in Release and Debug AppleClang runs. The historical one-allocation observation (192 bytes) did not recur and therefore has no owner backtrace; the release gate remains inconclusive rather than being declared closed.

harness.behavior: thread-local scoped global new/new[] allocation counting

test_change.test: Grainfield prepared processing stays allocation-free across block sizes

coverage.priming: one note-on process before arming the probe; MIDI and output buffers cleared before measurement

backtrace_diagnostic.method: temporary copy of rt_allocation_probe.cpp with backtrace_symbols_fd at allocation recording
backtrace_diagnostic.result: No process-path allocation occurred, so no owner stack was captured. The diagnostic run initially counted Catch2 INFO/reporting allocations because diagnostics were formatted while the probe scope was active; the committed matrix test snapshots counts before leaving the probe and formats diagnostics afterward.

validation.full_ctest: 19 of 20 runnable Grainfield tests passed; editor test was not built because Pulp::view is unavailable in this SDK configuration

conclusion: Keep the realtime allocation gate inconclusive. Current Release and Debug matrix evidence is clean, but it cannot prove that the prior intermittent 192-byte event was impossible. Close only after recurrence is captured and owned or after an independently justified cross-toolchain closure policy accepts the bounded evidence.
next_action: Run the committed matrix test in the supported CI/toolchain set and capture a backtrace immediately if any nonzero count recurs.
